A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OTQMS research despite retitling and substantial reformatting. Their complete texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original OTQMS accuracy results, ablations, shot-sensitivity experiments, and training-time and sample-usage measurements, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds an Office-Home multi-task experiment in Section 5.7 and Table 4.

M1.justification: V3 adds a multi-task adaptation that treats each task as the target in turn and recomputes source transfer quantities during training (Section 5.7). The core OTQMS optimization and dynamic resampling remain. Moving source pretraining outside Algorithm 1 and explicitly specifying random sampling do not establish changes to those underlying steps.

E1.justification: V3 adds a multi-task learning scenario across the four Office-Home domains, with tasks serving as both sources and targets. DomainNet, Office-Home, Digits, and the illustrative CIFAR10 experiment were already covered in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched main, LoRA, Digits, and ablation experiments. The added multi-task experiment uses a Single-task/no-transfer control corresponding to the existing Target-Only approach.

E3.justification: The new multi-task experiment introduces evaluation with rotating target-task roles using ViT-Small. Existing experiments retain the stated 20% test split, few-shot sampling protocol, Adam learning rate, and five-epoch early-stopping setting; the PDFs do not establish that these retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The domain-preference analysis receives a limited quantitative revision in its preference matrix. It otherwise moves from v1 Section 5.7 to v3 Appendix F with the same questions and interpretations. Static-versus-dynamic, shot-sensitivity, and data-efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The matched shot-sensitivity plots retain their uncertainty displays. Neither version specifies experimental run counts, seeds, error-bar definitions, confidence levels, or significance tests; no change in statistical reporting practice is established.

E6.justification: V3 Table 4 adds multi-task results averaging 83.5% for OTQMS and 71.4% for Single-task training. The domain-preference heatmap changes some values, including Sketch's preference for Quickdraw from 0.092 to 0.11. Matched benchmark and appendix table scores remain unchanged; the new multi-task scores are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equation 6 reverses the central risk from KL(learned || target) to KL(target || learned). Section 3 replaces the Cramer-Rao-bound lemma with MLE asymptotic normality. Appendix C adds a Lagrangian/Taylor derivation in Lemma 10, explicit regularity conditions, and corrections to signs, factors, and remainder terms. These substantially revise the mathematical foundation, although the leading transfer-quantity formulas remain.

C1.justification: The central optimal-transfer-quantity contribution and headline accuracy/data-efficiency claims remain. V3 recasts the theoretical basis as asymptotic high-dimensional statistics, elevates the existing dynamic strategy into an explicit contribution, and adds a claim of applicability to multi-task learning.

C2.justification: V3 Section 4.3 newly explains how scarce target data makes parameter estimation inaccurate and why dynamic resampling is intended to alleviate this problem. It also explains the approximation supplied by pretrained source parameters. The principal bias-variance and domain-preference interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly documents random sampling, negative-log-likelihood loss, the empirical-Fisher interpretation, and uniform-step search for transfer quantities. These clarify existing operations. Conversely, v3 removes v1's code and supplementary-materials access statement and link.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to Wasserman, Martens, PipeFisher, and Transfusion to support statistical and implementation arguments, and removes Langley's paper-writing reference. Existing transfer-learning positioning is largely retained, with its detailed discussion moved to Appendix B.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper and substantially revises the theoretical narrative and practical-algorithm explanation. Full main-text related work becomes a short summary plus Appendix B, while domain-preference discussion moves to Appendix F. These reorganizations extend beyond renumbering or added experimental content.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to predominantly single-column layout. V1's bias-variance illustration, Figure 3, is removed; shot plots change from a 2-by-2 arrangement to four panels across. Domain-selection heatmaps are relocated, enlarged, and numerically annotated, and a multi-task results table is added.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects specific sign and factor errors, revises the KL risk definition, and supplies missing derivation steps, improving the coherence and inspectability of the theoretical argument. Clearer explanation of dynamic estimation and the multi-task experiment provide additional value. Removal of the code/supplementary-materials link weakens reproducibility information, but the documented corrections and clarifications support a modest net improvement.
